Computers and programs
Vocabulary

Program: Ordered instructions processed by a computer.

Input: Values supplied before processing.

Output: Values produced by those instructions.

Meaning

A processor follows instructions; it does not infer the meaning you intended. Read x, multiply by a factor, then add an offset. Changing the order generally changes the answer. The lesson executes Python in a downloaded runtime; the browser displays its recorded values.

Purpose

Tracing one instruction at a time lets you locate where a wrong result began.

Calculation

output = x × factor + offset

Worked case

Inputs: [2, 3, 1]. Result: 7. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Transfer case

Inputs: [-2, 4, 1]. Result: -7. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Explain

Which operation happens first in this program?

Multiplication, followed by offset addition

The program explicitly specifies multiplication before addition. Parentheses and program structure determine order.

Debug

Treating a program as a live formula instead of a sequence.

Predict the result if the offset is added before multiplication: (2 + 1) × 3 = 9. Explain the difference.

Mini-project

Write a three-instruction calculator and test a negative input.

Variables, loops, functions and objects
Vocabulary

Variable: A name bound to a value.

Loop: Instructions repeated for each item.

Function: A reusable procedure with parameters and a returned value.

Object: An instance whose attributes retain state.

Meaning

Assignment stores a result when its line runs. A for loop visits list items in order. An if condition can skip an addition. Functions have call-local names; returning a value does not make a local name global. Methods update the attributes of a particular object. Use the real Python labs to inspect those scopes.

Purpose

These operations turn mathematical recipes into reusable programs.

Calculation

total = sum of values greater than zero

Worked case

Inputs: [2, -1, 3]. Result: 5. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Transfer case

Inputs: [1, -3, 2]. Result: 3. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Explain

Why does the negative value not change this total?

The condition fails, so the addition is skipped

The iteration still visits every value. The condition controls only the indented addition.

Debug

Resetting total to zero inside the loop.

A loop that resets total every iteration returns only the last included item. Move initialization before the loop.

CPU, RAM, GPU and storage
Vocabulary

CPU: Executes general instructions.

RAM: Working memory holding active data.

GPU: A processor suited to many parallel operations.

Storage: Persistent data such as files and checkpoints.

Meaning

A saved file lives in storage. Loading it places data in RAM. A CPU or GPU performs computations on accessible data. Moving data to a GPU has a cost; parallel hardware does not automatically accelerate a small operation. The payload of an array is its element count times bytes per element, distinct from object and runtime overhead.

Purpose

Memory estimates help you select batch sizes without mistaking disk space for RAM.

Calculation

payload bytes = rows × columns × bytes per element

Worked case

Inputs: [2, 3, 4]. Result: 24. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Transfer case

Inputs: [4, 3, 8]. Result: 96. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Explain

Does this payload estimate include the entire Python runtime?

No; it counts only numeric element storage

Object metadata, allocator behavior, code, and runtime memory are additional.

Debug

Calling 24 payload bytes the total process memory.

A float64 array with the same shape uses twice the payload of float32, but process memory need not double.

Loading and cleaning data
Vocabulary

Row: One observation in a table.

Missing value: A field with no observed value.

Duplicate: A repeated record under a chosen identity rule.

Meaning

Inspect a loaded table before modeling: columns, types, missing values and units. In this toy table we drop a missing measurement and one exact duplicate, then calculate the mean. Real cleaning needs domain knowledge: repeated measurements may be legitimate, and removing missing rows can bias a sample. Fit any learned imputation rule using training data only.

Purpose

Silent data errors can make a correct learning algorithm solve the wrong problem.

Calculation

cleaned mean = sum of retained unique values / retained count

Worked case

Inputs: [2, 4]. Result: 3. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Transfer case

Inputs: [1, 5]. Result: 3. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Should every repeated value always be deleted?

No; duplicate identity and meaning must be checked

Two people can have the same measurement. This exercise explicitly assumes an exact repeated record.

Algebra and graphs
Vocabulary

Slope: Change in y per unit change in x.

Intercept: y when x equals zero.

Graph: Pairs of x and y drawn on axes.

Meaning

A line y = mx + b combines a scaled input with an offset. With m = 3 and b = 1, x = 2 gives y = 7. Negative x follows exactly the same operations. Raising b shifts the line vertically; changing m alters its steepness. Read the axes rather than assuming every rising line has slope one.

Purpose

Linear models and neural layers repeatedly use this operation.

Calculation

y = m × x + b

Worked case

Inputs: [2, 3, 1]. Result: 7. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Transfer case

Inputs: [-2, 3, 1]. Result: -5. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Explain

What changes when only b increases?

The line shifts vertically while slope stays fixed

The added offset changes every y by the same amount.

Debug

Confusing slope with the height at one point.

Compare y = 3x + 1 and y = 3x + 2 at x = 0 and x = 2. The difference is always one.

Mini-project

Probability, mean and variance
Vocabulary

Mean: Sum divided by count.

Population variance: Mean squared distance from the mean.

Probability: A number from zero to one describing uncertainty.

Meaning

For equally likely outcomes, probability is favorable outcomes divided by all outcomes. The mean describes a center. Variance measures spread using squared deviations, so negative and positive deviations do not cancel. This lesson computes population variance, dividing by n. Estimating variance from a sample commonly uses n - 1 instead.

Purpose

Models reason about uncertainty and normalize data using statistics.

Calculation

μ = Σx/n; variance = Σ(x - μ)²/n

Worked case

Inputs: [1, 2, 3]. Result: 0.6666666666666666. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Transfer case

Inputs: [2, 2, 2]. Result: 0. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Explain

Why square deviations before averaging?

So distances do not cancel and larger deviations weigh more

Raw deviations from the mean sum to zero; squaring measures their magnitude.

Debug

Dividing by n - 1 while labeling the result population variance.

For [1,2,3], mean = 2, squared deviations = [1,0,1], variance = 2/3. For a fair die, P(even) = 3/6.

Mini-project

Vectors, matrices and dot products
Vocabulary

Vector: An ordered list of coordinates.

Matrix: Numbers arranged along rows and columns.

Dot product: Sum of products of corresponding coordinates.

Meaning

Pair each input with the weight at the same position. Multiply each pair, then sum. For x = [2,3] and w = [4,-1], products are 8 and -3, giving 5. A dot product requires equal lengths. Matrix multiplication repeats compatible dot products; it is different from multiplying elements at matching positions.

Purpose

Neurons and dense layers calculate weighted sums with dot products.

Calculation

x · w = x₁w₁ + x₂w₂

Worked case

Inputs: [2, 4, 3, -1]. Result: 5. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Transfer case

Inputs: [4, 4, 3, -1]. Result: 13. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Explain

What must match for a vector dot product?

The two vector lengths

Lengths define how many coordinate pairs exist; values may differ.

Debug

Using Python list concatenation instead of numeric addition.

[2,3] + [4,-1] concatenates lists in Python. It does not calculate a dot product.

Derivatives and chain rule
Vocabulary

Derivative: Local rate of change of an output with an input.

Intermediate: A value between input and final output.

Chain rule: Multiply derivatives along a composition.

Meaning

Let u = s × x and y = u². First find dy/du = 2u, then du/dx = s. Multiply to get dy/dx = 2s²x. At x = 2 and s = 3, u = 6 and the derivative is 36. The derivative is a sensitivity, not the output y. A small input change Δx gives approximately derivative × Δx change in y.

Purpose

Backpropagation applies this rule across many connected operations.

Calculation

dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx) = 2s²x

Worked case

Inputs: [2, 3]. Result: 36. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Transfer case

Inputs: [-1, 2]. Result: -8. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Explain

How do local derivatives combine along this path?

Multiply them

A small x change first changes u; that u change then changes y. The two scale factors multiply.

Debug

Reporting y as though it were dy/dx.

At x = 2, s = 3, y = 36 and dy/dx = 36 happen to match. At x = 1 they are 9 and 18.

Symbolic versus learned systems
Vocabulary

Rule: Behavior explicitly written by a programmer.

Parameter: An adjustable value in a model.

Learning: Using data to choose parameters.

Meaning

A rule-based system applies specified logic. A learned system adjusts parameters from examples. Both can be AI. Fit a line through two observed input-target pairs: slope is target difference divided by input difference. This fitting is a tiny learning example; good training accuracy alone does not prove future accuracy.

Purpose

The distinction helps you choose a transparent rule or a data-driven model for a problem.

Calculation

learned slope = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁)

Worked case

Inputs: [1, 3, 2, 6]. Result: 2. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Transfer case

Inputs: [1, 3, 3, 9]. Result: 3. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Explain

What makes this slope learned?

It is calculated from observed examples

The examples determine the parameter; the fitting algorithm is still programmed.

Assuming ML eliminates human design decisions.

Identify which parts are designed: features, model family, objective and split. Which value is fitted?

Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning
Vocabulary

Supervised: Learn from input-target examples.

Unsupervised: Find structure without task target labels.

Reinforcement: Learn behavior using rewards from interactions.

Meaning

Predicting a labeled price is supervised learning. Grouping similar unlabeled observations is unsupervised. Choosing actions from rewards is reinforcement learning. The sign-group demonstration is a deliberately specified grouping rule, not a trained clustering model. Count the groups present, and distinguish the demonstration from the learning categories.

The feedback available determines the type of learning problem.

number of nonempty sign groups

Inputs: [1, 2, 3]. Result: 1. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Which task uses rewards from actions?

Reinforcement learning

Rewards evaluate behavior over interactions; they are not the same as a target label for every observation.

Explain why this visualization groups values without fitting any parameters.

Features, labels and predictions
Vocabulary

Feature: Input information available when making a prediction.

Label: The observed target used to learn or evaluate.

Prediction: A model output for an input.

Meaning

If hours studied is a feature and exam score is the label, a toy model might predict score = 10 × hours + 20. A prediction can be wrong even if its calculation is correct. Inputs must be available at prediction time; including the final score as an input leaks the answer.

Purpose

Keeping these roles separate prevents meaningless evaluations.

Calculation

prediction = weight × feature + bias

Worked case

Inputs: [2, 10, 20]. Result: 40. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Transfer case

Inputs: [3, 10, 20]. Result: 50. The app exposes intermediate operations step by step.

Explain

Can the final exam score be an input when predicting that same score before the exam?

No; it is unavailable and leaks the target

Future or target information cannot support the intended prediction task.

Confusion matrix, precision, recall and F1
Vocabulary

TP: A positive case correctly predicted positive.

FP: A negative case incorrectly predicted positive.

FN: A positive case incorrectly predicted negative.

F1: Harmonic balance of precision and recall.

Meaning

Precision asks how many predicted positives are correct: TP/(TP+FP). Recall asks how many actual positives are found: TP/(TP+FN). F1 = 2TP/(2TP+FP+FN). For TP = 3, FP = 1, FN = 2, precision is 0.75, recall is 0.6 and F1 is 2/3. Undefined zero denominators must be reported explicitly.

Purpose

Different errors have different costs; accuracy alone can hide them.

Calculation

F1 = 2TP/(2TP + FP + FN)

Vocabulary

Underfitting: The model fails to capture useful structure.

Overfitting: The model captures training-specific patterns poorly transferable to new data.

Stable softmax
Vocabulary

Logit: A raw score before probability normalization.

Softmax: Exponentials normalized to sum to one.

Stabilization: Subtract a shared maximum before exponentiation.

Meaning

Exponentiating logits like 1000 directly can overflow. Subtracting their maximum preserves softmax probabilities because the common scale cancels. For logits [1000,1001], use [-1,0]. Purpose

Stable normalization prevents avoidable numerical failures.

Calculation

Initialization
Vocabulary

Fan-in: Number of incoming connections.

Symmetry: Units behaving identically because their parameters match.

He scale: A variance-based choice commonly used with ReLU.

Meaning

Identical zero weights in a hidden layer can make units receive identical updates, preventing useful specialization. Random initialization breaks symmetry. He normal initialization uses variance 2/fan-in, hence standard deviation sqrt(2/fan-in), under its assumptions. The panel calculates the scale, not a random sample. One initializer is not suitable for every activation.

Purpose

Appropriate scale helps prevent unstable signals and gradients.

Calculation

Inputs: [8]. Result: 0.5. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Vocabulary

Broadcasting: Align trailing dimensions and expand axes of length one.

Autograd graphs
Vocabulary

Graph node: An operation or value in a computation.

Gradient path: A route from a parameter to the loss.

Meaning

For y = s × x × x, x appears on two multiplication inputs. Each route contributes to the derivative, so dy/dx = sx + sx = 2sx. Training versus inference
Vocabulary

Training mode: Behavior used while learning parameters.

Inference mode: Behavior used for prediction after training.

Dropout mask: Values deciding which activations are retained.

Meaning

Training can use randomness such as dropout and batch statistics. Inference generally disables dropout and uses learned normalization statistics. In inverted dropout, a kept activation is divided by its keep probability during training; inference returns the activation unchanged. A fixed mask is shown here for reproducibility, not sampled randomly.

Purpose

Forgetting the mode can produce inconsistent predictions.

Calculation

training output = x × mask/(1 - drop probability)

Worked case

Inputs: [2, 0.5, 1]. Result: 4. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Transfer case

Inputs: [2, 0.5, 0]. Result: 0. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Explain

What does inverted dropout do during inference?

It returns the activation without dropping or rescaling it

Training scaling already preserves the expected activation.

Vocabulary

Residual: Prediction minus target.

MAE: Mean absolute residual.

MSE: Mean squared residual.

Meaning

Purpose

The objective defines what training tries to improve.

MSE = mean(error²); MAE = mean(abs(error))

Binary and categorical cross entropy
Vocabulary

Target probability: Probability assigned to the observed class.

Cross entropy: Negative log probability of the target, averaged as specified.

Meaning

For a binary target y, BCE = -y log(p) - (1-y) log(1-p). With p = 0.8 and y = 1, loss is -log(0.8). With y = 0 it is -log(0.2), a larger penalty. Categorical cross entropy for a one-hot target is -Σ yᵢlog(pᵢ), selecting the true-class probability. Natural logs are used here.

Purpose

Confident wrong predictions deserve larger loss than uncertain wrong predictions.

Calculation

BCE = -y log(p) - (1-y) log(1-p)

The probability of the true class

The target selects the observed class; confident prediction of another class increases loss.

Stable logits losses
Vocabulary

Logit loss: Cross entropy calculated directly from raw scores.

Log-sum-exp: A stabilized log of a sum of exponentials.

Purpose

Stable objectives preserve useful values at confident predictions.

BCE(z,y) = max(z,0) - zy + log1p(exp(-abs(z)))

Gradient descent
Vocabulary

Gradient: Sensitivity of loss to a parameter.

Learning rate: The multiplier controlling update size.

Meaning

For L(w) = w², the derivative is 2w. The update w_new = w - η(2w) moves opposite the derivative. Starting at 2 with rate 0.1 gives 1.6, lowering loss from 4 to 2.56. Starting at -2 gives -1.6. A large step can overshoot; a small loss on one step does not prove convergence.

Purpose

Training changes parameters to improve the chosen objective.

Calculation

w_new = w - η × dL/dw

Worked case

Transfer case

Inputs: [-2, 0.1]. Result: -1.6. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Explain

Why subtract the derivative in this update?

To move in the local direction of decreasing loss

A negative derivative causes the weight to increase; the direction follows local loss sensitivity.

SGD, momentum and Adam
Vocabulary

SGD: An update using a sample or mini-batch gradient.

Momentum: Retains a velocity across updates.

Adam: Uses first and second gradient moments with bias correction.

Meaning

Plain SGD uses w - ηg. This momentum convention uses v_new = βv_old + g, then w - ηv_new. Adam maintains m and v as exponential averages, corrects their early-step bias, then scales m_hat by sqrt(v_hat)+epsilon. The panel compares SGD, momentum and a freshly initialized first Adam step; it does not reuse the momentum velocity as Adam state.

Purpose

Optimizer state changes how a sequence of gradients affects weights.

Vocabulary

Schedule: A rule changing learning rate during training.

Epoch: One traversal of the training set.

Meaning

An exponential schedule sets η_k = η_0 × decay^k. Starting at 0.1 with decay 0.5 gives 0.025 at epoch two. Local derivatives
Vocabulary

Local derivative: Sensitivity of one operation to its immediate input.

Upstream derivative: Sensitivity arriving from later operations.

Meaning

Composition: One operation takes the result of another.

Path derivative: Product of sensitivities along one path.

Vocabulary

Delta: Loss sensitivity to a layer preactivation.

Forward pass: Compute values using current parameters.

Estimate the derivative of f(x) = x² with (f(x+h)-f(x-h))/(2h). At x = 2 and h = 0.001, the result is about 4. Large h can introduce truncation error for general functions; very small h can cause floating-point cancellation. Avoid nondifferentiable corners when comparing smooth derivatives.

Gradient checks catch algebraic or implementation errors.

central difference = [f(x+h)-f(x-h)]/(2h)

Inputs: [2, 0.001]. Result: 4. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Inputs: [-1, 0.001]. Result: -2. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Is the smallest possible h always the most accurate?

No; rounding and cancellation can dominate

Finite precision creates a tradeoff between truncation and rounding error.

Checking ReLU at zero as if it had a unique ordinary derivative.

Vanishing and exploding gradients
Vocabulary

Vanishing: Repeated factors make sensitivity approach zero.

Exploding: Repeated factors increase sensitivity greatly.

Meaning

Backpropagation multiplies local factors. Four factors of 0.5 produce 0.0625, while four factors of 2 produce 16. Actual networks have matrix Jacobians and multiple routes, so this scalar path is an illustration. Activation saturation, initialization, normalization and architecture affect gradient behavior; clipping limits magnitude but does not restore a vanished signal.

Purpose

Poor sensitivity can prevent earlier layers from learning usefully.

Calculation

path gradient = product of local factors

Worked case

Inputs: [0.5, 4]. Result: 0.0625. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Transfer case

Inputs: [2, 4]. Result: 16. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Explain

Does clipping an exploding gradient recreate a vanished gradient?

No; these are different problems

Clipping caps a large magnitude; it does not amplify a near-zero gradient path.

Debug

Assuming depth alone guarantees either failure mode.

A chain of factors equal to one preserves its sensitivity at any tested depth.

Dataset loaders and training loops
Vocabulary

Dataset: A collection exposing examples and targets.

Loader: A mechanism assembling batches.

Training loop: Repeated forward, loss, gradient and update operations.

Meaning

For each batch: read features and targets, compute predictions, calculate loss, clear stale gradients, compute current gradients, then update parameters. Evaluation uses held-out data without fitting to it. A loader chooses batching and ordering; it does not automatically perform training. The final partial-batch policy is explicit in this count example.

Purpose

A correct loop connects the mathematics to reproducible computation.

Calculation

updates per epoch = ceil(example count / batch size)

Worked case

Inputs: [5, 2, 1]. Result: 3. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Transfer case

Inputs: [5, 3, 2]. Result: 4. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Explain

Should validation batches update the fitted model?

No; validation evaluates chosen behavior

Using validation data to fit parameters compromises its intended role.

Batching and shuffling
Vocabulary

Shuffle: Reorder examples before forming batches.

Seed: A control making a pseudorandom order reproducible.

Meaning

Shuffling changes which examples appear together and in what order, while preserving each example-target pairing. In ordinary epoch-based training, every training example should be visited according to the loader policy. The batch count is unchanged by reordering. Never shuffle inputs independently of their labels. Evaluation usually does not need shuffled order.

Purpose

Order can change SGD updates; reproducibility requires recording it.

Calculation

updates = ceil(N/batch) × epochs regardless of permutation

Worked case

Inputs: [6, 2, 1]. Result: 3. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Transfer case

Inputs: [6, 4, 1]. Result: 2. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Each input and its own target

Breaking alignment changes the learning task into incorrect labels.

Regularization and weight decay
Vocabulary

Regularization: A constraint or penalty discouraging undesirable fitting behavior.

L2 penalty: An objective term proportional to squared weights.

Meaning

Adding λw²/2 gives penalty gradient λw. An SGD update becomes w_new = w - η(g_data + λw). With no data gradient, w shrinks toward zero. Coupled L2 gradient and decoupled weight decay can differ under adaptive optimizers; do not treat every framework option as identical.

Purpose

Regularization trades training fit against a preference for simpler parameter values.

Calculation

w_new = w - η(g_data + λw)

Worked case

Inputs: [2, 0.1, 0.5, 0]. Result: 1.9. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Transfer case

Inputs: [-2, 0.1, 0.5, 0]. Result: -1.9. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

No; adaptive gradient scaling changes their relationship

The penalty gradient may enter adaptive moment calculations, while decoupled decay is applied separately.

Dropout
Vocabulary

Drop rate: Probability an activation is removed during training.

Inverted scaling: Divide retained values by the keep probability.

Meaning

With activation 2 and drop rate 0.5, a kept value becomes 4 and a removed value becomes 0. Their expectation is 2 under the specified Bernoulli mask. At inference, return the unchanged activation. This visualization uses a fixed mask so the arithmetic can be predicted; actual training typically samples masks.

Purpose

Dropout changes training behavior and can reduce reliance on particular activations.

Calculation

training output = activation × mask/(1-p)

Worked case

Inputs: [2, 0.5, 1]. Result: 4. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Transfer case

Inputs: [2, 0.5, 0]. Result: 0. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Explain

Why scale the kept activation?

To preserve its expected value under the dropout distribution

Individual outputs differ; only the expectation is preserved.

For input 2 at p = 0.5, average the two equally likely outputs 0 and 4.

Batch normalization
Vocabulary

Batch mean: Mean of activations for one feature in the batch.

Batch variance: Spread around that mean.

Gamma and beta: Learned scaling and shifting.

Meaning

For one feature with batch values 1 and 3, mean is 2 and biased variance is 1. Normalize the first value to -1 when epsilon is zero; gamma two gives -2 with beta zero. A small positive epsilon prevents division by zero. Training uses batch statistics; ordinary evaluation uses running statistics. Framework running-variance conventions need separate care.

Purpose

Normalization behavior depends on batch statistics and training mode.

Calculation

output = gamma × (x - mean)/sqrt(variance + epsilon) + beta

Worked case

Inputs: [1, 3, 2, 0]. Result: -2. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Transfer case

Inputs: [2, 4, 1, 0]. Result: -1. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Explain

Which statistics does ordinary inference typically use?

Saved running statistics

Recomputing fitted statistics from test data changes evaluation behavior.

Initialization in training
Vocabulary

Signal scale: Magnitude propagated across layers.

Gradient scale: Magnitude of loss sensitivity.

Meaning

Initializer assumptions interact with activation functions and fan-in. He variance 2/fan-in is commonly paired with ReLU. An unstable initial signal can make training fail before meaningful fitting begins.

Early stopping
Vocabulary

Patience: How long to wait without a sufficient validation improvement.

Best checkpoint: Saved parameters from the best eligible validation result.

Meaning

Track validation loss after training epochs. If it worsens while training loss keeps falling, stop according to a stated patience policy and restore the best checkpoint. This panel selects the lowest validation-loss epoch, using the earliest epoch for ties; it does not claim to simulate every patience rule. Test data must not choose the stopping point.

Purpose

Stopping controls training duration without optimizing directly on the test set.

Calculation

best epoch = argmin validation loss, with earliest tie

Worked case

Inputs: [0.8, 0.4, 0.6]. Result: 2. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Transfer case

Inputs: [0.3, 0.4, 0.5]. Result: 1. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Explain

Which data should choose the early-stopping epoch?

Validation data

A test-based stopping decision makes test performance part of selection.

Vocabulary

Model state: Parameters and persistent model buffers.

Optimizer state: Moments, velocities and update count.

Resume metadata: Epoch, scheduler, data order and random state as needed.

Exact training continuation also needs optimizer state and relevant scheduler/random/data-loader state. Here a saved scalar weight is restored for a prediction; the changed current weight is deliberately ignored.

Training diagnostics
Vocabulary

Diagnostic: An observation that guides investigation.

Baseline: A simple comparison model or rule.

Nonfinite value: NaN or infinity, usually indicating a numerical failure.

Meaning

Track training/validation losses, prediction distributions, per-class errors, gradient magnitudes and data alignment. A large loss gap is evidence to investigate, not a unique diagnosis. Compare with a simple baseline and inspect examples. If loss becomes nonfinite, stop and locate the first failing operation rather than displaying a success badge.

Purpose

Diagnostics connect a failed outcome to a testable cause.

Calculation

observed loss gap = validation loss - training loss

Worked case

Inputs: [0.05, 0.9]. Result: 0.85. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Transfer case

Inputs: [0.4, 0.45]. Result: 0.05. Intermediate operations are available in the app.

Explain

Does one loss curve identify a unique fix?

No; test possible causes with data and intermediate values

Different failures can produce similar curves; targeted checks distinguish them.

Debug

Ignoring a NaN because the previous epoch looked good.

Check input types, labels, stable loss, learning rate and gradients in a deliberate order.
